title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row' while the same file's erased_at tombstone keeps it
evidence:
+--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
+--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
...
+  -- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
+  -- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
detail: Header comment documents row deletion; the erased_at column comment (and the spec's W3 'tombstone-not-delete' ruling) documents row retention as a suppression record. GDPR-erasure semantics stated two contradictory ways in one file.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the header bullet to describe the tombstone: fields/token wiped, erased_at set, (vacancy,email) kept as suppression record until vacancy close.

title: Spec says the serializer skips hidden inputs; shouldSkipControl never checks type 'hidden'
detail: The claimed hidden-skip exists only via the underscore-prefix naming convention. Any present or future hidden input without a '_' prefix is silently persisted into draft PII, and no test pins hidden exclusion.
recommended_fix: Add an explicit `if (type === "hidden") return true;` to shouldSkipControl and a serializer test pinning that hidden controls never leave the page.

title: Suggested Review Order still points reviewers at 'data-resume-token', which round 3 removed from the DOM
evidence:
+  Blocker (autocapture leak): the resume token no longer sits in ANY DOM
+  attribute — PostHog autocapture reads element attributes into
vs
+- Marker, banner, data-resume-token, backdated timing stamp.
+  [`form_pages.gleam:387`](../../server/src/application/form_pages.gleam#L387)
detail: Round 3 moved the token to window.__rtResumeToken precisely because a DOM attribute leaked into autocapture, yet the review-order section (current guidance, not changelog history) still names data-resume-token.
recommended_fix: Update the review-order bullet to reference the CSP-nonced inline global (window.__rtResumeToken) instead of data-resume-token.

title: Spec task checklist schema omits erased_at and still describes erasure as delete_by_token
evidence:
+- [x] `supabase/migrations/<ts>_create_application_draft.sql` — `application_draft(id uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(), vacancy_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES vacancy(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, email text NOT NULL, fields jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}', continue_token text NULL, last_link_sent_at timestamptz NULL, resumed_at timestamptz NULL, submitted_at timestamptz NULL, created_at/updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), UNIQUE(vacancy_id, email))`
vs
+  erased_at          TIMESTAMPTZ,
detail: The execution checklist's canonical schema was never updated after the W3 tombstone ruling; the shipped migration carries erased_at. Checklist and artifact disagree on the table definition.
recommended_fix: Amend the task line to include erased_at and rename delete_by_token to reflect the tombstone (wipe + stamp) semantics.

...
+  // Applicant-facing copy — KEEP IN SYNC with server/src/application/

detail: The test name claims a cross-language sync guarantee, but it can only assert the JS constants. A form_copy.gleam edit passes everything while the applicant-facing strings diverge.

title: Capability gate checks fetch/CustomEvent/JSON but the continue-click chain uses Promise.prototype.finally
detail: Browsers with fetch but without Promise.finally (older Edge/Safari) pass the gate, then the click handler throws constructing the chain and the button stays disabled with no status copy.
recommended_fix: Replace .finally with a .then pair (or add finally to the gate) so the button re-enables on every browser the gate admits.

title: saveNow learns nothing from non-2xx: oversize (413) payloads retry on every step change and pagehide forever
detail: The closed-vacancy answer terminally disables the saver, but a terminally-unsaveable payload (over 64 KB, over key/value caps) just falls through silently and is re-POSTed on every subsequent step change and tab close.
recommended_fix: Treat repeated non-2xx saves as terminal for the current payload (disable until the payload changes), or client-side pre-check the 64 KB/key caps before sending.

title: Permanent server rejection of a save has no terminal path — silent indefinite retry (client email gate is looser than shared/email.is_valid)
detail: An applicant whose plausible-looking email passes the client regex but fails the server's stricter rule gets zero draft persistence with no signal, and the dead POST repeats on every step change/beacon. Only closed:true has a terminal state; other permanent rejections retry forever.
recommended_fix: Mirror the shared rule client-side (or accept the server's verdict): treat an ok:false/4xx that is not closed as terminal for this payload — suppress further saves until a field actually changes, or give up after N identical rejections.

title: Capability gate doesn't cover Promise.prototype.finally, but the continue-button chain ends in .finally
detail: Browsers with fetch/CustomEvent/JSON but no Promise.prototype.finally (Edge 14–17, Safari 10.1–11.0) pass the gate, then the click handler throws synchronously constructing the chain (.finally is not a function): the button stays disabled, no status copy appears — while the fetch itself has already fired.
recommended_fix: Add Promise.prototype.finally to the capability gate, or replace .finally with re-enabling the button inside both the .then and .catch arms.

title: Migration header says erasure 'removes the row', contradicting the tombstone design documented in the same file
evidence:
Line 12-13: '--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.'
vs line 41-46: '-- Erasure tombstone: a confirmed Art. 17 deletion wipes fields/token but
-- keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close so a still-open form
-- tab's next auto-save hits the upsert's erased_at guard instead of
-- silently re-creating the PII payload.' — and server/src/application/sql/erase_draft_by_token.sql confirms: 'tombstone, NOT a hard delete ... the (vacancy, email) key is kept as a suppression record until the retention sweep removes it at vacancy close' (UPDATE ... SET fields = '{}', continue_token = NULL, erased_at = now()).
detail: Stale pre-W3 comment: the spec change log (Perkins r1, W3) changed erasure to a tombstone that keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close, but the header bullet still claims the endpoint removes the row. Comment-only, but it misstates the GDPR erasure semantics of the table it documents.
recommended_fix: Reword the header bullet to match the tombstone, e.g. 'Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that wipes fields/token and tombstones the row (see erased_at); the retention sweep removes the key at vacancy close.'

title: Migration header comment contradicts the shipped token-lifecycle and erasure design (stale capability-model documentation)
evidence:
Migration header: "* Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row." and "-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request)." — contradicted within the same file by the erased_at column comment ("keeps the (vacancy, email) key until vacancy close") and by the in-chunk spec change log: "W1: tokens mint at SAVE time (upsert arg 4, COALESCE keeps existing)" and "W3: erasure is a tombstone (fields/token wiped, erased_at set, email kept as suppression record until vacancy close)" (_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-form-save-resume-f3.md).
detail: The schema's own documentation of a capability-token auth model misstates when tokens are minted (save-time, not first link request, so most rows are NOT NULL-token) and what erasure does (tombstone, not row delete). Future security/compliance audits reading the migration will reason from a wrong threat model.
recommended_fix: Update the header comment to state tokens mint at save time (COALESCE-preserved) and erasure writes an erased_at tombstone retaining (vacancy_id, email) as a suppression record until vacancy close.

title: Migration header comment misdescribes the shipped erasure and token-mint design
evidence:
--   * Erasure — the continue email carries a self-service delete link
--     (POST /apply/:code/draft-erasure/:token) that removes the row.
...
-- continue_token is 288 bits of URL-safe entropy (wisp.random_string(48)),
-- same capability model as application.erasure_token: the token IS the
-- auth. Partial unique index — most rows have NULL (token minted lazily on
-- the first "email me a link" request).
detail: Both statements are stale vs the shipped design: erase_draft_by_token.sql tombstones ("tombstone, NOT a hard delete") and the file's own erased_at comment agrees; tokens mint at SAVE (upsert_application_draft.sql: "minted at SAVE time"), so most rows will NOT have NULL. Migrations are immutable once merged — last chance to fix.
recommended_fix: Before merge, edit the header to say erasure tombstones (fields/token wiped, email kept as suppression record until vacancy close) and that tokens mint at save time.

title: DOMContentLoaded bootstrap passes the Event object as `env`, silently disabling the saver on that path
detail: As a listener, initBrowser receives the Event as env; Event has no .document so it returns before activating. Unreachable today (both script tags are defer → readyState 'interactive'), failure direction is safe, but the sibling files' arg-less initBrowser has no such trap and _initBrowser tests never exercise the listener path.
recommended_fix: Wrap the listener: root.document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () { initBrowser(); });

title: Applicant-facing copy lives in two places with comment-only sync; the Gleam half is dead code
detail: The five form_copy.gleam constants (draft_prep_note, draft_continue_*) are referenced by no SSR render — grep shows only a comment in form_view.gleam:124 uses the name. Strings match today, but no test pins Gleam↔JS equality, and the repo already has a single-source pattern: SSR-emitted data-* attributes read by form.js's upload preflight.
recommended_fix: Acceptable as-is per REVIEW_HINT_STEPPER precedent; if touched again, prefer emitting the strings as data-* attributes on the prep block so form_copy.gleam is the real source, or pin equality in a test.

title: Serializer does not skip hidden-type inputs, despite the spec's task text claiming it does
detail: Harmless today: the only hidden inputs in the SSR form are _-prefixed (_form_loaded_at at form_view.gleam:632, honeypot _website), so the `_` guard already covers them. But a future non-underscore hidden field would silently persist into drafts, contradicting the documented contract.
recommended_fix: Add `if (type === "hidden") return true;` to shouldSkipControl for defense-in-depth, and pin it with a form_draft.test.js case.

title: Continue-button chain uses Promise.finally, which the N10 capability gate does not check
detail: Browsers with fetch but no Promise.prototype.finally (Safari 10.1–11.0) pass the gate; the click handler then throws TypeError synchronously after `button.disabled = true`, leaving the button stuck disabled with no status copy. Near-zero 2026 impact, but it contradicts the gate's stated ancient-browser purpose.
recommended_fix: Replace `.finally(...)` with re-enabling the button inside both `.then` and `.catch`, or add `typeof Promise !== "undefined" && typeof Promise.prototype.finally === "function"` to the capability gate.

title: Continue-button non-2xx branch (Perkins r3's named 413 fix) has no pinning test — every wired failure test uses an HTTP-ok response
detail: The r3 changelog calls out the 413-envelope misrender ('Link sent' + phantom application_draft_saved) as a fixed regression, yet the exact branch that fixes it (`!res.ok → {ok:false}`) is never driven. Reverting it ships green.
recommended_fix: Add a wiring test with `responder: { ok: false, body: {} }` asserting status shows CONTINUE_FAILED and no rt:draft-saved is dispatched.

title: saveNow transient-failure path untested — nothing pins that a failed save stays dirty and is retried on the next step change
detail: The designed failure mode (silent retry via dirty state) is the core resilience behaviour of the save path. A regression that marks the payload sent optimistically, or swallows the retry, would pass all current tests while drafts silently stop persisting after any transient error.
recommended_fix: Add a wiring test: first fetch rejects (or ok:false without closed) → fire step-changed again → assert a second fetch with the same payload.

title: rt:draft-saved → application_draft_saved relay registration in apply_analytics.js is untested (marker gating + listener wiring)
detail: Producer side (announce-once in form_draft.js) and the consent-gated capture queue are both pinned, and event names are cross-pinned, but the relay registration itself — including the marker whitelist — has zero coverage. Restricting the markers or dropping the listener would silently kill the feature's headline saved-draft metric with all tests green.
recommended_fix: Export an _initBrowser(env) seam like form_draft.js's and add a test: fire rt:draft-saved on a form marker → capture queued; on confirmation marker → no listener registered.

title: Stepper resume-start wiring (form-resume → firstIncompleteIndex) untested at init level; only the pure function is pinned
evidence:
form_stepper.js:351-356:
          : marker === "form-resume"
            ? firstIncompleteIndex(sectionEls)
            : 0,
initBrowser is not exported; form_stepper.test.js covers firstIncompleteIndex (3 tests incl. complete-draft→last-section and hidden-wrapper boundary) and shouldActivate('form-resume'), but no test drives the start-step selection itself.
detail: The acceptance criterion 'stepper starts at first incomplete section' depends on this one ternary. It mirrors the pre-existing (equally untested) firstErrorIndex wiring, so it follows repo convention — residual risk is low but the wiring could regress (e.g. marker typo) with green tests.
recommended_fix: Extract the start-step choice into an exported pure predicate (marker, sectionEls) and pin the three marker arms, or accept and document the convention.

title: pagehide beacon ack-dedupe branch untested — no test asserts an already-acknowledged payload is not re-beaconed
detail: Impact of a regression is one redundant idempotent upsert per page life (harmless server-side), hence note-level — but the branch exists to prevent exactly that and is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Extend the continue-click or acknowledged-save wiring test: fire pagehide after the ack and assert beaconCalls.length stays 0.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
evidence: Traceability over this chunk: P0 behaviours 100% (never-leave-page serializer contract: form_draft.test.js shouldSkipControl/serializeForm pins; debounced save happy path + brand-checked timers: form_draft_wiring.test.js; form.js resume-guard anti-spam black hole: form.test.js; migration schema: server/test/integration/draft_integration_test.gleam, present in repo). P1 ≈85% — FULL: email gate, closed-vacancy disable, beacon flush, prep-swap + capability gate, outcomeEvent('form-resume') + funnel-suppression pin, event-name/cross-file contracts, copy-voice pins; PARTIAL: continue-button flow (non-2xx branch NONE), saveNow failure/retry (NONE), rt:draft-saved relay registration (NONE), stepper resume-start wiring (NONE). P2/P3 gaps: beacon ack-dedupe. Overall ≥80%.
detail: P0 fully covered and overall coverage exceeds 80%, but P1 sits at ~85% (below the 90% PASS bar): four verifiable gaps, three of them in the save/continue/analytics-relay wiring that form_draft_wiring.test.js exists to pin — including one named r3 regression fix (413 envelope) shipped without its own pin.
recommended_fix: Add the four wiring tests above (non-2xx continue failure, failed-save retry, relay listener via exported seam, beacon dedupe). That lifts P1 to ~100% and the gate to PASS.

title: handle_continue_link doc says ok:false only on Resend failure, but upsert failure also returns ok:false (200, not 500)
detail: The doc comment promises ok:false only when the Resend call fails and 500s for DB failures, yet an upsert DB failure yields ok:false with HTTP 200. Either the comment or the behaviour is wrong.
recommended_fix: Align the two: either return 500 on upsert failure per the doc, or amend the doc to state upsert-failure also answers ok:false/200.

title: strip_draft_on_submit does not clear last_link_sent_at, so submitted drafts keep counting toward the hourly fan-out bound
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET fields = '{}'::jsonb,
    continue_token = NULL,
    submitted_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND email = lower($2)
-- vs claim_continue_link_send.sql:
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d2
    WHERE d2.email = lower($2)
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at IS NOT NULL
      AND d2.last_link_sent_at > now() - interval '1 hour'
-- vs erase_draft_by_token.sql which does: last_link_sent_at = NULL,
detail: Erasure clears last_link_sent_at; submit does not. A recently-emailed-then-submitted draft still occupies a slot in the 3-per-hour cross-vacancy count for the same recipient, skewing the bound.
recommended_fix: Add last_link_sent_at = NULL to strip_draft_on_submit's SET clause, matching the erasure tombstone.

title: upsert_application_draft ON CONFLICT does not bump updated_at while strip_draft_on_submit maintains it manually
evidence:
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
  SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields,
      continue_token = COALESCE(
        application_draft.continue_token,
        EXCLUDED.continue_token
      )
-- contrast strip_draft_on_submit.sql:
    submitted_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
detail: strip_draft_on_submit sets updated_at = now() explicitly, proving the column exists and is maintained by hand. The hot upsert path (every debounced save) never touches it, so updated_at goes stale on the most-updated rows.
recommended_fix: Add updated_at = now() to the ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET clause, or document why draft saves must not move updated_at.

title: Draft strip runs before file-resolution work in finalise_application; a later failure leaves the applicant with neither draft nor a perceived-successful submit
detail: The strip is placed ahead of document owner resolution (and presumably uploads). If any later step fails the request, the user sees a failed submission while the saved-draft PII is already wiped and the continue token killed.
recommended_fix: Move the strip to the end of finalise_application (after all fallible steps), or confirm nothing after this point can fail the submission.

title: Send-failure path clears the cooldown stamp, also removing the row from the hourly fan-out count
detail: clear_last_link_sent sets last_link_sent_at = NULL, which both lifts the 10-minute cooldown and drops the row from the 3-per-hour cross-vacancy count. During a Resend outage every retry re-claims and re-clears, so the bounds effectively vanish exactly when sends are failing.
recommended_fix: Acceptable as designed, but consider a separate last_link_attempted_at for the fan-out count so failed sends still rate-limit claim attempts.

title: Save endpoint reports ok:true when the 500-draft per-vacancy cap silently discards the upsert
evidence:
OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
-- handler:
                    Ok(_) -> {
...
                      wisp.json_response(json_ok(True), 200)
detail: When the cap is hit and no (vacancy,email) row exists, INSERT...SELECT inserts nothing and RETURNING yields zero rows; the handler matches Ok(_) and answers ok:true. The applicant's answers are not saved while the UI claims they are.
recommended_fix: Match on the returned row count: Ok(pog.Returned(_, [])) after a non-empty upsert should log and return a distinct response (e.g. ok:false) instead of ok:true.

title: Five form_copy constants have no Gleam reference anywhere in the diff (only consumed by form_draft.js)
evidence:
pub const draft_prep_note: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_button: String = "Email me a link to continue"
pub const draft_continue_sent: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_needs_email: String = ...
pub const draft_continue_failed: String = ...
-- header comment: 'The prep-note swap and the continue-link button strings ALSO live in `priv/static/form_draft.js` (plain static JS can't import Gleam) — KEEP IN SYNC'
detail: draft_prep_note, draft_continue_button, draft_continue_sent, draft_continue_needs_email and draft_continue_failed are defined in Gleam but only the static JS uses these strings; nothing server-side renders them. They exist solely as a sync-prone duplicate source of truth.
recommended_fix: Either reference them server-side (e.g. inject into the page for JS to read) or drop the Gleam copies and keep a single canonical home in form_draft.js.

title: Redundant COALESCE on continue_token in two queries whose own clauses guarantee non-NULL
evidence:
RETURNING COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token;
-- same statement already ran: SET continue_token = COALESCE(continue_token, $3)
-- and in list_resumable_draft_tokens.sql:
SELECT email, COALESCE(continue_token, '') AS continue_token
FROM application_draft
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND submitted_at IS NULL
  AND continue_token IS NOT NULL;
detail: In claim_continue_link_send the SET clause makes continue_token non-NULL before RETURNING is evaluated; in list_resumable_draft_tokens the WHERE continue_token IS NOT NULL does the same. Both COALESCEs are dead and mask future regressions.
recommended_fix: Return continue_token directly in both queries; the guarantees are already enforced by the SET/WHERE clauses.

title: Post-submit save/beacon can INSERT a fresh unsubmitted draft when no draft row exists for (vacancy, email)
evidence:
INSERT INTO application_draft (vacancy_id, email, fields, continue_token)
SELECT $1::uuid, lower($2), $3::jsonb, $4
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND d.email = lower($2)
  )
  OR (
    SELECT count(*) FROM application_draft d
    WHERE d.vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  ) < 500
ON CONFLICT (vacancy_id, email) DO UPDATE
  SET fields = EXCLUDED.fields,
      continue_token = COALESCE(
        application_draft.continue_token,
        EXCLUDED.continue_token
      )
  WHERE application_draft.submitted_at IS NULL
    AND application_draft.erased_at IS NULL
detail: The submitted/erased guards only fire on the ON CONFLICT branch (existing row). If the applicant submits with no draft row for (vacancy, submit-email) — email edited after the last save and submitted inside the 800 ms debounce, prior saves failed while the pagehide beacon succeeds, or a stale second tab — the late save INSERTs a new draft with full PII, submitted_at NULL and a live continue_token after the final POST made the application row the system of record. claim_continue_link_send will then email a continue link for an already-submitted applicant and the resume page renders their pre-submit PII; only the application_vacancy_id_email_key constraint stops a duplicate submit. The diff's own strip comment ('a late beacon / still-open tab after the final POST... must not bring the PII back') claims this vector is closed.
recommended_fix: Add AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM application a WHERE a.vacancy_id = $1::uuid AND a.email = lower($2)) to the INSERT's WHERE clause so a draft can never be created for a (vacancy, email) that already has a submitted application.

title: Zero-row upsert (per-vacancy 500-draft cap reached for a new email pair) is reported to the client as a successful save
detail: When the INSERT...SELECT's count(*) < 500 guard fails for a new (vacancy, email) pair, upsert_application_draft returns Ok with zero rows; handle_save_draft matches Ok(_) and answers ok:true, so form_draft.js sets lastSentPayload and stops retrying — the applicant's progress is silently never persisted. In handle_continue_link the same zero-row outcome flows into the claim (also zero rows) and answers ok:true, so the UI shows 'Link sent — check your inbox' with no email ever sent. Reachable once a vacancy accumulates 500 drafts (abuse with distinct emails, since drafts persist until vacancy close).
recommended_fix: Match on pog.Returned(count, _) instead of Ok(_): log a warning (or Sentry-flag) on zero-row upserts from non-tombstone causes, and consider returning ok:false so the client doesn't acknowledge an unsaved state.

title: Resume page and draft write endpoints skip the check_max_applications gate the pristine form applies
evidence:
handle_resume:
          case application_handler.is_accepting_applications(vacancy) {
            False ->
              form_pages.view_closed_vacancy_page(
                vacancy,
                posthog_client.public_capture_key(config.posthog),
              )
              |> form_view.to_html_response

vs handle_get_form (application_handler.gleam:64):
          case check_max_applications(db, vacancy) {
            True ->
              form_pages.view_closed_vacancy_page(vacancy, posthog_api_key)
              |> form_view.to_html_response
            False ->
              form_view.view_application_page(vacancy, posthog_api_key)
detail: handle_get_form and handle_post_form render the closed page when the vacancy hits its max_applications cap, but handle_resume only checks is_accepting_applications — a continue-link holder on a capped vacancy gets a fully fillable restored form whose submit then bounces to the closed page, wasting their effort. lookup_accepting_vacancy likewise keeps accepting draft saves and continue-link requests for a vacancy whose form is already closed at capacity.
recommended_fix: Run check_max_applications in handle_resume (render the closed page when capped) and in lookup_accepting_vacancy (return the closed JSON payload), or add a comment making the divergence deliberate.

title: New public draft write + token-gated erasure endpoints have no Cloudflare edge rate limit despite mirroring the /erase abuse model
evidence:
http.Put, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "draft"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_save_draft(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "continue-link"] ->
      draft_handler.handle_continue_link(req, ctx.config, code)
    http.Get, ["apply", code, "resume", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_resume(req, ctx.config, code, token)
    http.Get, ["apply", code, "draft-erasure", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_erasure_confirm(req, ctx.config, code, token)
    http.Post, ["apply", code, "draft-erasure", token] ->
      draft_handler.handle_erasure_delete(req, ctx.config, code, token)

and deployment/terraform/cloudflare-rate-limits.tf:58 (the only http_ratelimit rule):
    expression  = "(starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \"/erase/\") or starts_with(http.request.uri.path, \"/dsar/\"))"
detail: The module header states the security/abuse model 'mirrors the erasure endpoint', but /erase//dsar/ carry a 5 req/10s per-IP edge block while the draft-erasure POST (same profile: anonymous, token-only, deletes applicant data) and the two unauthenticated write endpoints have no per-IP edge throttle. In-app bounds (64 KB body cap, 500 drafts/vacancy, 10-min cooldown, 3/hour fan-out) bound email spam and total stored rows, but unauthenticated DB-write rate and token-endpoint traffic (email-scanner prefetch bursts, enumeration noise — the /erase rule's stated targets) are unbounded at the edge.
recommended_fix: Extend the cloudflare_ruleset http_ratelimit expression to cover /apply/*/draft-erasure/ (and consider the draft/continue-link writes), matching the /erase per-IP block.

title: PostHog session recording not disabled on token-bearing resume page — sanitize_properties scrub covers events only
evidence:
<> "capture_pageview:true,capture_pageleave:true,"
<> "opt_out_capturing_by_default:true,"
// F3: the resume page's URL carries the 288-bit continue token — a
// read-capability for applicant PII. Scrub it (and the draft-erasure
// sibling) from every URL-ish event property before anything leaves
// the browser; the token must never land in the analytics store
...
<> "sanitize_properties:function(p){"  — and a repo-wide grep of server/src finds no `disable_session_recording` / `session_recording` config anywhere. form_pages.gleam:435 renders this snippet on the resume page (`form_view.view_posthog_snippet(vacancy.short_code, posthog_api_key)` inside view_resume_page).
detail: sanitize_properties only amends event properties; PostHog session recording (rrweb) is a separate pipeline it does not filter. Compare the established precedent every other token-gated PII page follows (server/test/integration/gdpr_integration_test.gleam:1040-1052):

  |> list.key_find("cache-control")
